notes: behavioral-modes sets Claude's operational interaction style (brainstorm/implement/debug/review/teach/ship/orchestrate); it is user-invocable: false and fires on explicit mode-switch intent. Boundary distinguishes a mode switch from a concrete task that should go to an executor skill.

evals.prompt: Switch to brainstorm mode — I want to explore options for our notification system before we write any code.
evals.expected_output: Activates BRAINSTORM mode: asks clarifying questions first, offers at least 3 distinct alternatives with pros/cons, stays code-free, and announces the mode using the brainstorm output style.

evals.prompt: Treat the rest of this session as a review — go into review mode for the auth module.
evals.expected_output: Activates REVIEW mode: findings categorized by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), each with the why and a fix, and acknowledges what is done well — following the review output style.

IMPLEMENT-mode style applies (the word 'implement' is on Mode 2's auto-activate list), but behavioral-modes only sets interaction style — it must not perform the work. The build itself routes to the implement-feature executor.
